Prevention: Cut the leaf-top to reduce carry-over of eggs from the seedbed to the field before transplanting
Ensure synchronous and early planting especially in areas with a history of borer infestations
Harvest crops at ground level to remove the larvae in volunteer rice, plough and flood the field
Destroy crop residues after harvest to reduce overwintering borer population
Practice direct seeding to minimize pest infestation
Destroy alternative host and volunteer plants and burn infected rice straw
Apply correct amounts of nitrogen in 3 splits at basal, tillering and panicle initiation
Monitoring: Look for deadhearts or dead tillers that can be easily pulled from the base during the vegetative stages
Look for whiteheads during reproductive stage where the emerging panicles are whitish and unfilled or empty
Check for tiny holes on the stems and tillers; cut through to confirm presence of larvae
Check for frass or fecal matter inside the damaged stems
Take action when 10-30% of plants have typical symptom
Direct Control: Handpick and destroy egg masses at seedbed and transplanting
Raise level of irrigation water periodically to submerge the eggs deposited on the lower parts of the plant
Apply insecticides to coincide with larval emergence so larvae are killed before they enter the rice stems
Apply pesticides judiciously to conserve natural enemies (wasps, ants, beetles, bugs, ants, birds, dragonflies, damselflies, and spiders)

Bacillus thuringiensis based products to control young larvae

Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
